Repeat-item prediction and unseen-item recommendation require different populations. [Li et al.](https://irlab.science.uva.nl/wp-content/papercite-data/pdf/li-2023-repetition.pdf) distinguish targets previously consumed from first-time targets and show substantial accuracy differences. For repeat-capable next-item prediction, retain repeated targets and allow seen candidates; report repeat/explore results separately. For unseen-item diagnostics, exclude targets already present in the complete pre-target history and report exclusions and eligible counts. Filtering only the truncated encoder input permits older consumed items back into competition; describe that explicitly as window-based filtering. Never use post-target interactions to construct the prefix-seen set.

Recommended implementation rules, inferred from these task definitions: identify observations by category, user and prefix endpoint; collapse accidental duplicate observations, while retaining distinct real events even when their encoded sequences match. State whether aggregation weights events or users. Define eligible candidates before ranking, excluding padding and invalid IDs. For a diagnostic intended to match full-catalog eligibility, reject or deterministically replace supplied negatives outside that set, remove duplicate negatives and target collisions, and report resulting candidate counts. Preserve the pinned benchmark unchanged; report any corrected diagnostic separately. Sampled and full-catalog scores remain distinct estimands: [Rendle](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.02263) shows sampling can even reverse model comparisons.

Scores on prefixes whose targets participated in fitting measure training fit, even when inference receives only earlier interactions. Held-out evaluation requires targets excluded from fitting and contexts restricted to information available at prediction time. Label these populations separately and publish sampling seeds, filtering rules, denominators and aggregation choices; these implementation choices are central to [reproducible recommender evaluation](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11257-021-09302-x).
